title: Invited Near, Yet Held in Awe

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then the Lord said to Moses, 'Come up to the Lord, you and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel. You are to worship at a distance, but Moses alone is to approach the Lord; the others must not come near. And the people may not come up with him.'" - Exodus 24:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice the beautiful tension in God's words. He says "Come up" — an invitation to draw near. Yet in the same breath He sets careful limits: the elders worship at a distance, only Moses approaches, and the people stay below. God genuinely wants His people close, but His holiness is not something to be treated casually. Both truths stand together: He invites, and He is holy.

We often lose one side of this. Some think of God as so distant and severe that drawing near feels impossible. Others treat Him so casually that awe disappears altogether, as though He were merely a friendly companion. Scripture holds both — a God who calls us to come, and a God before whom we rightly bow. Losing either one shrinks our understanding of who He truly is.

Here is the wonder of the gospel. What Moses alone could do, Jesus has opened to all of us. Through His blood, we are invited to draw near with confidence into the very presence of God (Heb 10:19-22). The distance has been closed, not because God became less holy, but because Christ has made us clean. So come near today — freely, joyfully, boldly — but never carelessly. The One who welcomes you is still the Holy One.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I hold both truths — that God invites me near and that He is holy?
Has my approach to God become casual, or has fear kept me at a distance?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Holy Father, thank You that through Christ I can draw near to You with confidence. Keep my heart both bold in coming and reverent in worship, never casual about Your holiness. Amen.
